major_findings.title: The exact r2 candidate closure omits the validator, its adversarial tests, and the prior rejection receipt
major_findings.impact: An r2 receipt can be accepted after the validator, its tests, or the historical rejection record drift or are omitted.
major_findings.required_fix: Require a unique closed binding set that includes the validator, its tests, and every superseded historical FAIL receipt.

major_findings.title: The detached receipt can still be semantically self-signed
major_findings.impact: A local writer can self-fill role strings and a PASS verdict without a stable reviewer identity, exact review contract, zero-severity requirement, or temporal relation to the rejected predecessor.
major_findings.required_fix: Require exact schema and review ID, a stable reviewer agent identity, zero Critical and Major findings, a unique closed binding set, a review time later than the superseded rejections, and an explicit BLOCKED_NOT_AUTHORIZED boundary.

major_findings.title: A newer refresh source can mask another source that is stale at execution time
major_findings.required_fix: Check execution-time freshness against each source capture independently; use the latest source only for event ordering, not as the freshness baseline.

checks_that_passed: The candidate documents no longer self-declare PASS and the experiment uses a detached-receipt-only review result.
Without r2, the pending candidate cannot enter request_ready.
The validator recomputes the unique CEC target row, address, reporting year, and status from bound raw content.
The validator recomputes organization identity and exact public email from bound raw HTML and checks HTTP status and final URL.
Pre-execution freshness uses validation_now, and wrong status, duplicate target, unrelated content, wrong channel, non-200 status, and future or stale timestamps fail closed.
claim_boundary: This is a historical independent rejection of r2 attempt 1. It authorizes no contact, follow-up, quote, account access, submission, payment, delivery, publication, or external execution.
